sources.claim: RF package transitions, grounding, and the transmission-line interface are a coupled discontinuity and should be laid out as one structure.
sources.limits: Package-specific evaluation-board guidance and the selected connector datasheet override a generic launch pattern.
sources.title: Layout Guidelines for MMIC Components
sources.use: Give every launch an owner, preserve a short unbroken return path, and make launch geometry part of schematic, PCB, and first-article review.

sources.claim: Prefer curved RF turns; where a curved bend is used, a bend radius of at least three times the conductor width is the published layout guideline.
sources.limits: This is a layout guideline, not proof of broadband insertion loss; a first article or a more detailed model still owns performance.
sources.title: PCB Layout Guidelines for RF and Mixed-Signal
sources.use: Set an explicit radius-to-width policy and review every direction change, while treating the final impedance as a property of the ordered stackup.

sources.claim: Grounded coplanar routing uses adjacent grounded copper and stitching on both sides of the signal path to control the return structure.
sources.limits: A nominal via lattice is not evidence of the realized along-route pitch, and fence geometry does not replace reference-plane continuity review.
sources.title: PCB Layout Guidelines for RF and Mixed-Signal
sources.use: Require two-sided, route-following fence coverage and measure the saved plated returns along the complete route, including launch spans.

sources.claim: Controlled-impedance design requires a declared transmission-line structure and material/geometry inputs rather than width alone.
sources.limits: Use the current purchased standard and the fabricator's process data for contractual decisions; this card is only a routing reminder.
sources.title: IPC-2141A Design Guide for High-Speed Controlled Impedance Circuit Boards
sources.use: Treat impedance as a cross-section contract carried through fabrication evidence, not as an annotation applied after routing.

sources.claim: Controlled-impedance geometry must be calculated against a selected JLC layer stack and the matching structure type, using the manufacturer calculator inputs rather than a generic board thickness.
sources.limits: Public calculator output is planning evidence. The order preview and manufacturer engineering response remain the order-time authority.
sources.title: User Guide to the JLCPCB Impedance Calculator
sources.use: Lock the exact JLC stackup code, copper layer, reference layer, finished copper assumptions, width, and coplanar gap before layout is sealed.

sources.claim: JLC publishes named impedance stackups whose dielectric construction is the appropriate starting point for its controlled-impedance service.
sources.limits: Availability and process values can change; order-time evidence must echo the selected construction.
sources.title: JLCPCB Impedance Controlled PCB Stackups
sources.use: Record a named stackup rather than inferring dielectric height from the overall board thickness, and recheck it in the fabrication preview.

sources.claim: KiCad represents routed track arcs as native board items and supports rounded-corner routing workflows.
sources.limits: Router modes do not all edit existing arcs equivalently; the pipeline must verify its own deterministic emit/reopen path.
sources.title: KiCad PCB Editor documentation and board file format
sources.use: Preserve arcs as arcs through route emission, saved-board measurement, DRC, rendering, and release evidence instead of flattening them silently.

sources.claim: At microwave frequencies a routed interconnect is a distributed transmission line; geometry, materials, reference conductor, and discontinuities determine propagation and reflection.
sources.limits: Textbook models require the actual fabrication geometry and do not certify a manufacturer process by themselves.
sources.title: Microwave Engineering, transmission-line chapters
sources.use: Review the signal and return structure together and avoid treating a nominal trace width as a complete impedance specification.

sources.claim: Coplanar transmission-line behaviour depends on the complete conductor and dielectric geometry, including lateral ground spacing and conductor thickness.
sources.limits: Closed-form models are approximations and must be reconciled with the fabricator model and first-article measurement.
sources.title: Transmission Line Design Handbook, coplanar structures
sources.use: Keep the CPWG gap, width, copper thickness, dielectric height, and reference plane under one cross-section authority.
